Article Title: Oil prices today: Crude edges higher as US-Iran tensions revive supply concerns
Article Text:
The gains came after both benchmarks fell more than 2% in the previous session (representative image)

US threatens prolonged blockade of Iran

Strait of Hormuz remains key to oil supply

Demand concerns limit oil price gains

Oil prices edged higher on Friday as the United States threatened to maintain a naval blockade of Iran indefinitely, renewing concerns over crude supplies even as weaker demand forecasts and rising US inventories limited gains.Brent crude futures rose 9 cents, or 0.1%, to $87.16 a barrel by 0130 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 4 cents to $81.29 a barrel.The gains came after both benchmarks fell more than 2% in the previous session.Despite Thursday's decline, Brent was on track for a weekly gain of around 4%, while WTI was also headed for a rise of about 4%.Oil markets remained focused on the possibility of a prolonged conflict between the US and Iran and its impact on crude supplies.The United States said on Thursday that it could maintain a naval blockade of Iran indefinitely and would increase economic pressure on Tehran as ceasefire talks have stalled.US treasury secretary Scott Bessent warned of further measures against Iran.“Watch this space for more announcements coming next week because we are going to apply measures like have never been seen in the history of economic isolation on a country,” Bessent said in an interview with Newsmax's Rob Schmitt Tonight programme.The latest US position has heightened concerns that disruptions to oil flows through the region could persist.Iran has continued to restrict traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a major global oil shipping route that carried about 20% of the world's oil before the conflict, according to Reuters.Iran's newly appointed head of the Basij paramilitary force, Hossein Taeb, said the strait was “under the management and control of the Islamic Republic”, according to Iran's semi-official Fars news agency.The supply concerns were reinforced after two vessels belonging to state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company were attacked while transiting the strait on Thursday evening, according to the UAE state news agency WAM.The UAE government described the incident as an Iranian attack.Concerns over supply disruptions have been partly offset by a weaker outlook for global oil demand.Opec and the International Energy Agency lowered their forecasts for demand growth this week, while US crude inventories recorded their largest weekly increase in more than three and a half years.Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM, said the conflicting supply and demand factors were keeping the market from making a decisive move higher.“The result is a market that remains supported but struggles to break meaningfully higher while these opposing pressures remain in place,” he said, as cited by Reuters.For consumers and businesses, the direction of crude prices will therefore continue to depend largely on whether geopolitical supply risks outweigh concerns about weaker global demand and rising inventories.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures rose 9 cents, or 0.1%, to $87.16 a barrel by 0130 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 4 cents to $81.29 a barrel. The gains came after both benchmarks fell more than 2% in the previous session.

Article Title: 'Shadow transshipment network': US names India among 40 countries helping China evade tariffs
Article Text:
The report divided the more than 40 countries into three categories based on their economic relationship with China (representative image)

India placed in top-risk category alongside major economies

Peter Navarro warns India, Vietnam over tariff evasion

What is Chinese transshipment and why is the US targeting it?

US plans AI monitoring and tougher penalties

The US has put India among more than 40 countries it says face risks of becoming conduits for Chinese goods seeking to avoid American tariffs, potentially adding another complication to the ongoing trade negotiations between Washington and New Delhi.A new report by the White House Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy accused exporters in multiple countries of helping Chinese goods enter the US market through third countries, including by rerouting shipments, relabelling products or falsely declaring their country of origin.The report described the practice as the “Great Transhipment Scam” and warned that Washington would step up efforts to detect and penalise such shipments.The report divided the more than 40 countries into three categories based on their economic relationship with China and the risk of transshipment.India was placed in Tier 1, described as “Diversified Scale Leaders”, alongside Canada, the European Union, Israel, Japan, Mexico, South Korea and Taiwan.According to the report, these are large and diversified industrial economies where the risk of transshipment is embedded within otherwise legitimate trade flows.Tier 2, or “Significant Economic Integration with China”, includes Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Turkey and Vietnam.Tier 3, described as “Small, Opportunistic Targets”, includes Bangladesh, Cambodia, the Philippines, Singapore, Sri Lanka and the UAE.The classification does not by itself allege that all countries or their governments are deliberately facilitating tariff evasion. Rather, it identifies them as jurisdictions where US officials see varying levels of transshipment risk.Senior US trade adviser Peter Navarro specifically named India during a briefing on the report, warning that countries facing higher US tariffs could have an incentive to facilitate the routing of Chinese goods through their territories.“This is about the 40-plus countries that are enabling the transshipping, and as we impose higher tariffs on other countries, India, Vietnam, down the line, they're going to try this transhipment too,” Navarro said.He added that countries seeking lower tariffs should not use transshipment as a way to circumvent US trade measures.“The way to pay less is not to cheat; it is to stop dumping, respect intellectual property, drop your barriers to American goods and move towards reciprocity,” Navarro said.He further warned countries facilitating such trade that “preferential access to the American market is not a license to launder somebody else's exports.”Transshipment generally involves goods being routed through a third country before reaching their final destination. In legitimate trade, products can pass through several countries as part of complex supply chains.The concern raised by Washington is about shipments allegedly being rerouted or minimally processed to obscure their Chinese origin and avoid tariffs imposed on Chinese products.The report cited examples including Chinese electric motors being fitted into recliners in Vietnam.It also referred to so-called “screwdriver factories”, where imported components undergo only limited assembly before being exported as products originating from another country.US officials said such processes may not constitute the “substantial transformation” needed for a product to legitimately acquire a new country of origin.Washington is planning several measures to intensify its crackdown on suspected transshipment.According to the report, these include an executive order aimed at strengthening enforcement powers at US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and a new AI-based monitoring system described as a “detective border”.The system is intended to identify shipments carrying a higher risk of transshipment before they arrive at US ports.The US is also incorporating anti-transshipment provisions into new trade agreements. Officials said these clauses would carry penalties for countries that allow disguised Chinese goods to enter the US market through their territory.Importantly for India, officials indicated that such provisions could form part of future trade agreements, including a potential US-India deal.Under the proposed enforcement approach, if a shipment is subsequently found to have been transshipped, CBP could potentially seek tariffs retrospectively on a company's shipments going back one year, rather than limiting the action to the specific consignment identified.The report comes at a sensitive point in India-US trade negotiations over a reciprocal tariff agreement.Washington's concerns over Chinese goods entering the US through other countries could add another issue to negotiations already complicated by disagreements over India's trade and energy ties with Russia.US officials stressed that the report was “not about China” specifically, while identifying Vietnam, Cambodia, Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines as key transshipment hubs and warning that other countries facing higher tariffs could follow the same route.Officials declined to say how the findings could affect US President Donald Trump's expected meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, saying the report would inform the US Trade Representative's approach at the negotiating table.
Article Summary: India placed in top-risk category alongside major economies. White House Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy accused exporters of helping Chinese goods enter the US market through third countries. Report described the practice as the ‘Great Transhipment Scam’ Washington will step up efforts to detect and penalise such shipments.

Article Title: What Trump tariffs? Russia accounts for more than half of India’s crude oil imports
Article Text:
A sharp cut in Russian crude imports could raise India's oil import bill, disrupt refinery operations.

Russia a major supplier for India

What the US bill for sanctions on Russia could mean

What the Russia sanctions bill means

With Russia’s share in India’s oil imports progressively climbing up, any abrupt shift away from Moscow’s crude appears unlikely in wake of the fresh Trump tariff threat emerging from the US, says Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) in its latest report.According to GTRI’s analysis, Russia accounted for over 50% of India’s crude oil imports in July.“Russia supplied an estimated 52% of India’s crude-oil imports in July 2026, up from 48.6% in June. The estimate indicates that more than half of India’s imported crude now comes from Russia, sharply limiting New Delhi’s ability to reduce these purchases at short notice,” says GTRI founder Ajay Srivastava.Also Read | 100% tariffs: Why India may ignore Trump threat and continue buying Russian crude oil According to GTRI’s analysis, in June India imported crude oil worth $14.8 billion from all sources, of which $7.2 billion came from Russia. This translated into a Russian share of 48.6%.For July, the government released data showing India's overall imports from Russia at $8.9 billion but did not disclose how much of that consisted of crude oil. Since crude accounted for 82% of India's imports from Russia in June, GTRI applied the same proportion to July's figures, estimating Russian crude imports at around $7.3 billion.India's crude sourcing pattern has undergone a major transformation.India's dependence on Russian crude has risen sharply over the past few years. Russia's share in India's crude oil imports climbed from around 15% in 2022 to 30.3% in FY2025-26. This has only gone up in recent months amid the US-Iran war.At the same time, the combined contribution of Gulf suppliers has declined significantly, dropping from more than 55% in 2022 to below 30% by June 2026. The conflict involving Iran and the resulting disruptions to global supply chains further accelerated this shift, increasing the importance of Russian crude in meeting India's energy needs.The proposed US sanctions could leave India facing a difficult decision.If the proposed US legislation on Russian sanctions is enacted, India could be exposed to additional tariffs of up to 100% should it continue importing Russian energy.“The measure could force India to choose between reducing its Russian oil purchases and protecting its exports to the US,” says Srivastava.However, he notes that India has limited room to make an abrupt shift.“Replacing a supplier that now accounts for more than half of imported crude would be difficult, costly and potentially disruptive. Alternative suppliers may not be able to provide comparable volumes immediately or on equally favourable commercial terms,” he says.A sharp cut in Russian crude imports could raise India's oil import bill, disrupt refinery operations, widen the trade deficit and add to inflationary pressures. It could also increase the country's dependence on an already volatile West Asian region, Srivastava adds.According to the GTRI founder, India should continue buying Russian crude oil.“Discounted Russian crude has lowered India’s import costs, diversified its supplies and strengthened energy security. India should continue purchasing Russian oil as long as it remains commercially attractive and complies with applicable rules,” he says.“American tariff threats should not determine India’s energy policy. Differences with Washington should be addressed through firm negotiations, not unilateral concessions that raise India’s energy costs and weaken its strategic autonomy,” he adds.Also Read | US tariff threat on Russian oil: Bill a concern for India, but ‘talks have been reassuring’
Article Summary: Russia accounted for over 50% of India’s crude oil imports in July. A sharp cut in Russian crude imports could raise India's oil import bill, disrupt refinery operations. It could also increase the country's dependence on an already volatile West Asian region.

Article Title: CPI data: Retail inflation moves up to 4.45% in July; stays above RBI's target for second month
Article Text:
Inflation remained higher in rural India at 4.84%, while urban areas registered a lower rate of 3.96%.

July 2026 CPI inflation: Retail inflation for the month of July edged up to 4.45%. The All India Consumer Price Index (CPI), with 2024 as the base year, recorded a provisional year-on-year inflation rate of 4.45% in July 2026 compared with July 2025. Inflation remained higher in rural India at 4.84%, while urban areas registered a lower rate of 3.96%.This is above RBI’s target of 4% but within the range of 2-6%. Inflation in June stood at 4.38%.Based on the All India Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), provisional food inflation stood at 5.52% year-on-year in July 2026. Rural food inflation was estimated at 5.79%, whereas the corresponding rate for urban India was 5.05%.Housing inflation, measured on a year-on-year basis, was provisionally estimated at 2.22% in July 2026. Rural areas recorded housing inflation of 2.80%, while the urban housing inflation rate was lower at 2.01%.Earlier this month, the Reserve Bank of India had kept the policy rates unchanged while lowering the full year inflation forecast and raising its GDP growth projections.“The MPC noted that headline CPI inflation edged up above the target, as expected.The realised inflation for Q1, however, remained marginally lower than projections reflecting limited pass-through of cost pressures. The higher inflation is mostly on account of fuel and food with little signs of generalisation of price pressures so far. Core inflation excluding precious metals continues to be benign. As projected earlier, headline inflation is expected to rise further in the near term and peak in Q3:2026-27, primarily due to food and fuel, before moderating thereafter,” RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said in his policy statement.“Going forward, El Niño’s impact on temporal and spatial rainfall distribution continues to remain a major risk, although proactive supply management and adequate stock of foodgrains should provide comfort. Global oil prices have remained highly volatile with sharp two-way movements triggered by geopolitical developments, blurring the near-term outlook. Although generalised inflation pressures continue to remain modest so far, the risks of second-round impact of higher food, fuel and other input prices translating to broad-based inflation persist,” he said.“After considering all factors, CPI inflation for 2026-27 is projected to be 5.0 per cent with Q2 at 4.7 per cent; Q3 at 5.9 per cent; and Q4 at 5.5 per cent. Inflation for Q1:2027-28 is projected at 5.3 per cent with risks being evenly balanced. Core inflation is projected at 4.3 per cent for 2026-27. Core inflation excluding precious metals is projected to be lower, though it is likely to align with core inflation from Q4,” he added.
Article Summary: The All India Consumer Price Index (CPI), with 2024 as the base year, recorded a provisional year-on-year inflation rate of 4.45% in July 2026. Inflation remained higher in rural India at 4.84%, while urban areas registered a lower rate of 3.96%. This is above RBI’s target of 4% but within the range of 2-6%.

Article Title: ‘Fragile 5 to fastest growing’: PM Modi talks of India’s economic growth during Independence Day speech
Article Text:
PM Modi on Saturday led the country's 80th Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort.

India has become the world’s fastest growing major economy in the world in the last twelve years, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said during his Independence Day speech on Saturday.He also said that India has achieved this milestone despite being ranked among ‘Fragile Five’ a few years ago. “People's efforts have resulted in taking India from fragile five to major economy in the last 12 years,” he said.Talking about the dream to become a developed country by 2047, PM Modi said, “The world will be forced to look at India differently when the most populous country becomes a developed nation.”“India is dreaming big to touch new heights, we will make sure the country becomes developed by 2047,” he added.Also Check | PM Modi’s Independence Day Speech Live Updates PM Modi on Saturday led the country's 80th Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort amid patriotic fervour and extensive multi-layered security arrangements.For the first time in the history of India's Independence Day celebrations, 'Vande Mataram' was performed at the Red Fort during the 79th anniversary of Independence on August 15, followed by the rendition of the national anthem.The ceremony also marked 150 years of the enduring legacy of 'Vande Mataram'. Reflecting the theme, the floral arrangements on the Red Fort's ramparts featured the national flag at the centre, with the words 'Vande Mataram' displayed in Hindi on either side.This is PM Modi’s 13th consecutive Independence Day speech.Earlier in the day, the Prime Minister greeted the nation on Independence Day and paid homage to the country's freedom fighters, acknowledging their courage and sacrifices in securing India's freedom from colonial rule.Also Read | PM Modi’s 13th consecutive Independence Day Speech - Top Quotes In a post on X, PM Modi said that the ideals and aspirations of the freedom fighters continue to guide the nation as it moves towards the goal of becoming a Viksit Bharat. He also expressed hope that India's development journey would continue to gather greater momentum."Warm greetings on the occasion of Independence Day. We remember with gratitude the countless freedom fighters whose courage, sacrifice and unwavering commitment ensured the end of colonial rule. Their dreams continue to inspire us as we work together to build a Viksit Bharat. Powered by 140 crore Indians, our nation is scaling new heights of progress across different sectors. May this journey keep progressing at an even greater pace in the times to come", the Prime Minister posted on X.
Article Summary: India has become the world’s fastest growing major economy in the last twelve years, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said during his Independence Day speech on Saturday. He also said that India has achieved this milestone despite being ranked among ‘Fragile Five’ a few years ago.

Article Title: FMCG companies see recovery in consumption growth
Article Text:
Most of the quarter was marked by average 8-10% raw material cost hike

NEW DELHI: The consumer goods sector is seeing signs of a firmer consumption recovery, with volume growth becoming more visible across companies, even as cost pressures remain. This comes as the West Asia conflict has pushed up crude-linked inputs, packaging and freight costs for FMCG companies, raising concerns that the disruption could eventually weigh on demand.Major companies including Nestlé and Marico reported double-digit volume growth in June quarter, while HUL, Tata Consumer and Dabur also saw underlying volume momentum. After several quarters, in which growth was largely driven by inflation-led price increases, companies have reported a stronger consumer offtake, analysts and companies told TOI.Most of the quarter was marked by average 8-10% raw material cost hike, led by crude-linked inputs like packaging and edible oils with a rise in palm oil prices, which led to a pressure on margins. Most players resorted to selective price hikes and grammage cuts to offset cost escalation in June.“During the quarter, consumer demand remained strong, with industry navigating geo-political crisis and increased raw material costs by improving efficiency and limiting price hikes to around 3-5%.Also, urban consumption has nearly caught up with rural demand now. The industry is hopeful that festive season could be a growth driver for urban demand for rest of the year,’’ Mayank Shah, chief marketing officer, Parle Products said.Rural India continues to be a bright spot in the consumption landscape, outperforming urban markets for the eighth consecutive quarter. The gap between the two has narrowed with urban demand being driven by a strong performance of modern trade, quick commerce and premium products.“As per syndicated data, rural demand grew 170 basis points ahead of urban demand in the first quarter, with growth of 6.2% in rural versus 4.6% in urban markets. We believe this reflects a healthy broadening of India’s consumption story across urban and rural India,” Dabur India global CEO Mohit Malhotra earlier said.
Article Summary: Major companies including Nestlé and Marico reported double-digit volume growth in June quarter. HUL, Tata Consumer and Dabur also saw underlying volume momentum. Most of the quarter was marked by average 8-10% raw material cost hike.

Article Title: ‘No-go’ to ‘go-ahead’: PM Modi hails ‘Samudra Manthan' for deep-sea exploration in Independence Day speech
Article Text:
PM Modi said that nearly 99% of India's coastal waters had earlier been classified as "no-go areas".

‘No-go’ to ‘Go Ahead’ for Samudra Manthan

What is Samudra Manthan scheme?

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said India has opened up almost its entire coastal waters for exploration as part of efforts to identify new mineral reserves. PM Modi during his Independence Day speech said most of these coastal areas have now been opened for exploration under the 'Samudra Manthan' initiative.India is currently the world's third-largest consumer of crude oil, with an annual import bill of nearly $144 billion, equivalent to around Rs 13 lakh crore. Recent geopolitical conflicts that disrupted global oil and gas supplies have underscored the importance of increasing domestic production to meet the needs of the country's fast-growing economy.To speed up offshore exploration, the government approved Samudra Manthan – the National Offshore Exploration Scheme on July 31, 2026. The scheme has been allocated Rs 84,084 crore for Phase I, covering the period up to FY2030-31, with the objective of accelerating hydrocarbon exploration and production across the country.Also Read | Samudra Manthan explained: How India’s offshore oil & gas exploration scheme can be a game-changer PM Modi said a "flawed" approach in the past had prevented offshore exploration and added that areas once designated as "no-go zones" have now been converted into "go-ahead areas."Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort during the 80th Independence Day celebrations in New Delhi, the Prime Minister said that nearly 99% of India's coastal waters had earlier been classified as "no-go areas," effectively ruling out offshore exploration.He described this as a "poverty of thought" and said the government had decided to change that approach."We have now opened up those areas--previously off-limits--as "go-ahead areas," and we are actively pursuing exploration and the discovery of new reserves beneath the sea. Last year, we announced the "Samudra Manthan" initiative to advance this effort, and recently, we decided to accelerate the work by allocating ₹85,000 crore for this purpose," the Prime Minister said.India's offshore sedimentary basins are believed to contain substantial untapped hydrocarbon reserves. These basins are natural geological depressions where oil and gas accumulate over time. Unlocking these resources will require advanced exploration technologies, dependable geological data, modern drilling infrastructure and a robust domestic supply chain.Also Check | PM Modi’s Independence Day Speech Live Updates The Central government says a significant portion of India's future oil and gas reserves is expected to come from offshore regions. The country's eastern and western offshore basins include deepwater and ultra-deepwater zones extending to depths of nearly 3,000 metres. Together, these offshore areas are estimated to hold more than 5,600 MMTOE (Million Metric Tonnes of Oil Equivalent) of hydrocarbon resources.Emphasising the importance of energy security, PM Modi said India must focus on both alternative energy sources and more efficient use of energy.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said India has opened up almost its entire coastal waters for exploration as part of efforts to identify new mineral reserves. India is currently the world's third-largest consumer of crude oil, with an annual import bill of nearly $144 billion, equivalent to around Rs 13 lakh crore.

Article Title: India's big chip ambition: Can it become the world's next semiconductor hub?
Article Text:
India has taken definitive steps to establish itself as a credible player in the global semiconductor ecosystem.

India’s big semiconductor push

India’s 12 Approved Semiconductor Projects

India entering a game-changing phase?

Building India’s Chip Ecosystem

US, Taiwan, China, South Korea for chips: What about India?

Global Semiconductor market projections

Road ahead

India's Semiconductor opportunity: The numbers

With an outlay of over Rs 1.27 lakh crore India has launched the second phase of its ambitious semiconductor programme. Globally, a semiconductor supercycle is underway. If artificial intelligence is reshaping businesses world over, semiconductors are the building blocks for this shift.“In boardrooms across the semiconductor industry, the conversation has shifted. For years, leaders asked when the cycle would turn. Today, they’re asking how fast they can build. The real demand for AI suggests that the semiconductor supercycle may be underway,” KPMG said in its 2026 Global Semiconductor Outlook report.According to McKinsey, the semiconductor industry is now one of the world’s most profitable sectors. In fact, McKinsey estimates that the semiconductor industry could reach $1.6 trillion in revenue by 2030!One has to only look at the new records that US and South Korean stock markets have scaled driven by AI-led semiconductor demand. As semiconductors define the next big growth phase globally, where does India stand?Semiconductors sit underneath almost everything today: electronics, EVs, telecom, AI, data centres, defence, manufacturing.So having a self-reliant semiconductor ecosystem is an absolute necessity in the current globally uncertain economic and geopolitical environment.“If a country of India's size stays dependent on outside supply chains for something this fundamental, that's a real vulnerability, both economically and strategically,” Saurabh Agarwal, Partner, EY India tells TOI.What is India’s semiconductor plan? Can it compete against established players like the US, Taiwan, and South Korea?Through its mission, India is aiming to build an integrated semiconductor and AI ecosystem that spans chip design, fabrication, advanced packaging, research, talent, and computer infrastructure.India’s semiconductor push can be seen in two phases: Semicon 1 which had an outlay of Rs 76,000 crore, and the recently approved Semicon 2.0 which has a Cabinet nod of Rs 1,27,500 crore.So far, 12 semiconductor projects with investment commitments of over Rs 1.64 lakh crore have been approved; three facilities are already in commercial production.Meanwhile, semiconductor design capabilities are being expanded through skilling programmes, startup support and global partnerships.Semicon 1.0 provided fiscal support of up to 50% for silicon fabrication plants, compound semiconductor units, semiconductor assembly and testing facilities, and chip design.India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 prioritises domestic production of semiconductor equipment and materials, development of an end-to-end Indian semiconductor intellectual property stack.Industry estimates place the Indian semiconductor market at around $38 billion in 2023, rising to approximately $45-50 billion during 2024-25. The market is projected to expand further to $100-110 billion by 2030.The government hopes that India can develop the capability to design and manufacture chips catering to nearly 70-75% of its domestic demand by 2029.Building on this base, Semicon 2.0 aims to accelerate advanced chip manufacturing, with a defined roadmap for achieving 3-nanometre and 2-nanometre technology nodes.Semicon 2.0 focuses on six pillars: chip design, semiconductor equipment and materials, fabrication facilities, advanced packaging (ATMP/OSAT), research and development, and talent development.With this India is looking to position itself as a global semiconductor hub with an aim to strengthen the entire semiconductor value chain, attract more chipmakers, support indigenous intellectual property, advance semiconductor technologies.Experts see Semicon 2.0 as a potential gamechanger for India. Saurabh Agarwal, Partner of EY India says that while the first phase was about getting manufacturing capability off the ground, the second one is broader: design, fabs, packaging, materials, equipment, R&D and talent, all at once.“Done well, it can lift domestic value addition in electronics, pull in large investments, create serious engineering and manufacturing jobs, strengthen India's place in global supply chains, and push homegrown IP forward,” he says.The bigger shift is this: India stops being just a buyer of semiconductor technology and starts becoming a maker of it. Over the next ten years, semiconductors could do for India what software did over the last thirty, becoming a whole new engine of growth and self-reliance, Agarwal says.Experts also see the mission as a way to create high-skilled jobs in semicon industry and indirect employment across supply chains and supporting industries.“For electronics manufacturing, the initiative can help India move beyond assembly and increase domestic value addition by developing local component and semiconductor capabilities,” says Grant Thornton Bharat’s Krishan Arora.“From a technological self-reliance perspective, Semicon India 2.0 can reduce dependence on imported chips, strengthen supply-chain resilience, and build domestic expertise in semiconductor design, manufacturing, and advanced packaging,” he adds.But as Shivani Parashar says, ultimately, the success will depend not just on the number of projects India attracts, but on how much technology, IP, jobs and value India can build within the country.Saurabh Agarwal of EY India cautions that the next stage is harder. It's about going deeper, not just wider.“Fabs get the attention, but the real test is whether we build out the rest: equipment, specialty materials, gases and chemicals, research infrastructure, and skilled people,” he says.Experts believe India is uniquely positioned. Asked whether India would be able to match what China, South Korea have managed to achieve in their semiconductor journey, experts say India can create a differentiated semiconductor ecosystem.“India’s strongest competitive edge lies not in immediately matching Taiwan, South Korea, or China in advanced chip fabrication, but in building a differentiated semiconductor ecosystem,” says Krishan Arora, Partner and Leader Investment Advisory, Grant Thornton Bharat.The country combines a large pool of chip design talent, strong engineering capabilities, growing government support, rising domestic demand, and increasing interest from global companies seeking to diversify supply chains beyond traditional manufacturing hubs.“India’s biggest advantage in the semiconductor industry is its large pool of skilled engineers and strong R&D talent. Many of the world’s leading chip companies already run design and research centers in India, giving the country deep expertise in chip design and innovation. This strong talent base puts India in a unique position to build a competitive semiconductor ecosystem for the future,” he tells TOI.But Shivani Parashar notes that India’s semiconductor ecosystem is still heavily service oriented rather than product led. The challenge is not just having the engineering capability to design chips, but identifying large global markets and building products around them.“Commercialization remains one of the biggest gaps. The missing piece is converting India’s engineering talent into globally successful semiconductor businesses,” she says.Saurabh Agarwal believes India should pick the parts of the value chain where it can genuinely be world class.He says that India already has some real advantages: one of the deepest semiconductor design talent pools anywhere, a domestic electronics market that's growing fast, strong policy backing, solid engineering capability, and a geopolitical position that global supply chains trust.“That combination can make India a serious player in design, advanced packaging, compound semiconductors, specialty materials, equipment, and eventually mature node fabrication too. The goal isn't to beat the existing leaders at their own game, it's to become a partner the global ecosystem can't do without,” he tells TOI.The semiconductor sector is characterised by long development cycles, high capital requirements and sustained investment in research and development. Achieving India's semiconductor goals will therefore require a long-term strategy that addresses existing challenges while steadily building domestic capabilities. Experts note that capital outlay would be important.“From a policy perspective, consistency, speed and access to patient capital will be critical. Semiconductor projects have long development cycles and require significant investment, making predictable incentives, faster clearances and reliable infrastructure essential,” says Shivani Parashar of Counterpoint Research.“India also needs a stronger venture capital ecosystem capable of supporting 7-10 year development cycles, multiple tape-outs and deep-tech commercialization, without which many startups may struggle to move beyond first silicon,” she adds.She also believes that incentives should increasingly reward outcomes such as IP creation, product commercialization, production volumes, and revenue generation, rather than design activity alone.“The goal should be to move from being a design destination to becoming a creator and owner of globally competitive semiconductor products and intellectual property,” she concludes.According to Saurabh Agarwal, policy needs to move from handing out project specific incentives to actually building an ecosystem, backing R&D, forming global tech partnerships, and creating demand for what we design and make here.As the EY expert says: A few years ago, semiconductors in India were mostly a talking point. That's changed. We now have real projects on the ground.But that’s just a starting point to a long road.With its semiconductor mission, India has taken definitive steps to establish itself as a credible player in the global semiconductor ecosystem. But execution holds key and policies will need to continuously evolve for India to make a mark in the long-run.
Article Summary: India has taken definitive steps to establish itself as a credible player in the global semiconductor ecosystem. 12 semiconductor projects with investment commitments of over Rs 1.64 lakh crore have been approved; three facilities are already in commercial production. The government hopes that India can develop the capability to design and manufacture chips catering to nearly 70-75% of its domestic demand by 2029.

Article Title: Wholesale inflation eases to 9.8% in July
Article Text:
This is the third consecutive month when wholesale inflation has remained over 9%

NEW DELHI: Driven by softer energy prices, wholesale price index (WPI) based factory gate inflation moderated to 9.8% in July from a 27-month high of 9.9% in June, official data showed. In comparison, WPI stood at -0.8% in July last year.This is the third consecutive month when wholesale inflation has remained over 9%, as manufactured products and primary articles saw price acceleration. Deceleration in crude (27%) and mineral oil (32.4%) prices helped soften inflation in fuel and power segment to 20% from 27.4% in June.
Article Summary: WPI based factory gate inflation moderated to 9.8% in July from a 27-month high of 9.9% in June. Deceleration in crude (27%) and mineral oil (32.4%) prices helped soften inflation in fuel and power segment.

Article Title: Claude downloads surge 30x, Gemini doubles
Article Text:
Claude recorded the sharpest growth among major GenAI apps during the June quarter

NEW DELHI: India's AI-app race is getting more competitive. While ChatGPT continues to dominate user engagement and spending, Gemini is gaining ground and Claude is emerging as a fast-growing challenger, according to data from market intelligence firm Sensor Tower.Claude recorded the sharpest growth among major GenAI apps during the June quarter. Its downloads in India surged over 30-fold y-o-y to 8.5 million in Q2 2026, while consumer spending jumped nearly 19-fold to about Rs 62.2 crore. The rapid acceleration is significant, given Claude's relatively small presence in India until recently."Claude stands out with more consistent momentum, with downloads and monthly active users accelerating since early 2026, making it an increasingly notable player despite its smaller user base," said Eve Chen, insights analyst at Sensor Tower.ChatGPT, however, remains far ahead on monetisation. Consumer spending on the app stood at around Rs 112.8 crore during Q2, up 36% from a year earlier. Grok generated about Rs 20.4 crore, followed by Perplexity at Rs 5.8 crore and Gemini at Rs 1.8 crore.Google's Gemini is emerging as the stronger challenger on engagement. Downloads more than doubled to 18.1 million, while its share of time spent across GenAI apps climbed sharply to 18.7% from 4.9% a year earlier.
Article Summary: Claude recorded the sharpest growth among major GenAI apps during the June quarter. Its downloads in India surged over 30-fold y-o-y to 8.5 million in Q2 2026. Consumer spending jumped nearly 19-fold to about Rs 62.2 crore.

Article Title: With $52.3 billion raised, FCNR(B) scheme to close a month early
Article Text:
RBI introduced the special USD-INR forex swap facility on June 8, 2026

At the heart of the arrangement is RBI’s swap. Banks bring in dollars and RBI provides rupees in exchange.

MUMBAI: RBI has decided to close the special FCNR(B) scheme a month early on Aug 31 after banks mopped up $52.3 billion in deposits by Aug 13. The central bank’s decision follows a strong response to the facility, which was designed to bring foreign currency into India’s banking system at a time when dollar liquidity was a concern.RBI introduced the special USD-INR forex swap facility on June 8, 2026, covering FCNR(B) deposits, overseas foreign currency borrowings (OFCBs) and external commercial borrowings (ECBs). By Aug 13, banks had reported total inflows of $56.9 billion under the three components. FCNR(B) deposits accounted for $52.3 billion, while OFCBs and ECBs brought in $2.8 billion and $1.7 billion, respectively. Banks can swap the dollars raised with RBI until Sept 11. The facilities for ECBs and OFCBs will continue until Dec 31, as originally planned.Under the scheme, foreign banks have in many cases extended financing many times the amount of the initial deposit made by wealthy customers. Bankers said the challenges in deploying the proceeds in fixed-return long-term assets might have prompted the early closure.CS Setty, SBI chairman, said during an analysts’ meet that SBI had mobilised almost $6 billion of FCNR(B) deposits, alongside about $1 billion of OFCBs and $300 million of ECBs.That put total funding raised through the programme at roughly $7.3 billion, most of it through the bank’s foreign offices. Setty had earlier indicated that SBI could raise around $10 billion under the scheme. The proceeds would be used to retire bulk deposits of up to Rs 1 lakh crore.At the heart of the arrangement is RBI’s swap. Banks bring in dollars and RBI provides rupees in exchange. When the swap matures, the transaction is reversed, with the bank returning the rupees and receiving its dollars back. In economic terms, RBI absorbs much of the currency risk for the duration of the deposit, making the arrangement a form of state-provided currency insurance.
Article Summary: RBI introduced the special USD-INR forex swap facility on June 8, 2026. It covers FCNR(B) deposits, overseas foreign currency borrowings and external commercial borrowings. By Aug 13, banks had reported total inflows of $56.9 billion under the three components.

Article Title: Brain fitness: The next frontier after wellness apps?
Article Text:
Annamalai Chettiar, royal family of Chettinad with Patrick Porter on the eve of the longevity summit (Credit: Sanjay Hadkar)

MUMBAI: Somewhere between a sleep mask and a neuroscience lab, an American device that claims to compress a four-hour night's rest into 20 minutes is about to make its Indian debut, with a member of the Chettinad royal family as its local face. BrainTap USA is set to launch in India on Saturday at the two-day Longevity Summit India in Mumbai, where "mental mastery" shares the main stage with talk of gut microbiomes, peptides and cardiac coherence. The launch follows an MoU between BrainTap Technology in the US and BrainTap India, an initiative of the Royal Family of Chettinad, to bring the full BrainTap ecosystem, app, headset and a measuring device, into the country.BrainTap is built on a decades-old idea called brain entrainment: the theory that rhythmic external stimuli, light flickering at a set frequency, tones pulsing in each ear, can gently pull the brain's own electrical activity into step with them, the way a metronome pulls a wandering musician back on beat. The headset, developed over four decades by its founder, US neuroscientist Patrick Porter, delivers pulsed LED light through closed eyelids alongside binaural beats, isochronic tones and guided audio through a companion app.The idea is to shift users out of the anxious, overstimulated "beta" state most people live in and toward calmer alpha and theta brainwaves, the frequencies associated with relaxation, sleep onset and creative thinking. "When your eyes are closed, there's something called photobiomodulation," Porter said, explaining that light hitting the eyelids creates a flickering effect he calls a "frequency following response." It's the same basic principle, he says, that popularised binaural beats decades ago, except paired here with light and delivered through a closed, monitored loop rather than an open audio file on the internet.That loop is worth pausing on, because it maps onto a broader arc that wellness technology has followed over the past decade. The first generation of consumer wellness devices, the Fitbits, the early smartwatches, did one thing: they measured. Steps, heart rate, sleep duration, sometimes blood oxygen. The assumption was that visibility alone would nudge behaviour. A second generation went the other way and skipped measurement altogether, going straight to intervention: meditation apps, white-noise machines, weighted blankets, sleep headbands that simply played a programme regardless of who was wearing it or what state they were in. The frontier now being chased by companies like Whoop, Oura and a clutch of neurotech start-ups is a third stage, a closed loop that measures a person's baseline, uses that data to select or tailor an intervention, and then measures again to see whether it worked, in theory letting the system keep adjusting itself over time. BrainTap, as it stands today, sits closer to that third category than most competitors selling in India, but with an important caveat. While the company positions its NeuroChek Go device and AI layer as reading a user's state and recommending which of its library of sessions to use, the underlying sessions themselves don't dynamically change based on what the device measures. The protocol is, in Porter's own words, "already hardwired." The system points a user toward a different pre-built session based on the parameters measured before the intervention.Annamalai Chettiar, whose family is bringing the ecosystem to India, framed the appeal in more personal terms. "The most important aspect of longevity is the mind," he said. "If you can transform the mind, you've taken the first and most basic step. I slept barely five hours last night, yet after 25 minutes on this, I'm as fresh as if I'd had a full night. That's how fascinating these protocols are." His family's involvement, he said, grew out of years spent researching wellness technologies before settling on BrainTap as, in his words, among the best available in a crowded field.In India, the product will be sold in three tiers: the app alone, the app bundled with the headset, and a top tier that adds NeuroChek Go, a thumb-held sensor that takes roughly five minutes to read what the company describes as seven neurological parameters, including "brain voltage" and a biological-age estimate benchmarked against a database of some 40,000 prior users. That data, along with anything pulled in from a connected wearable such as an Oura ring or Whoop strap, feeds a recommendation engine trained on Porter’s own accumulated body of guidance, which then suggests which of the company's roughly 3,000 audio-visual sessions, spanning sleep, focus, sports recovery, women's health and other categories, a user should try next.On launch day at the summit ( thelongevitysummitindia.com ) the app, headset and a one-year subscription will be offered at a discounted price. Another option, a three-month subscription at a much lower cost is also on offer, users should notice improved sleep within that window, the company said. A rental model, hiring the device for a few months through the institute rather than buying outright, is also being planned, alongside a two-day experiential seminar this weekend where visitors can try the headset before deciding.Porter's pitch leans heavily on reframing sleep itself. "People mistake hours in bed for sleep," he said. "Sleep is a sport, we need to train for it, we need to think about it. It's not something to be avoided." He argues the real neurological requirement isn't total hours but architecture: roughly one hour of deep sleep to clear the brain's waste-clearing lymphatic system, and two hours of REM sleep to consolidate memory and process the day, benchmarks he says most people, sleeping in fragmented, poorly timed cycles, never actually hit regardless of how long they're in bed. He points to earlier work with professional athletes, including what he describes as a long-standing relationship with NFL quarterback Tom Brady, and to an in-house, unpublished, study with a Major League Soccer team's training staff, which he says found that 20 minutes on the device could approximate four hours of physical recovery. "We have 4,000 clinics using it in the US right now," he said, citing what BrainTap says is a library of 72 published studies conducted on the device across sleep, cognition, stroke and mood-related outcomes.That evidence base is more substantial than what most consumer wellness gadgets can point to, though it varies quite a bit in rigour. A pilot at AIIMS Bhopal recorded measurable rises in gamma, beta and alpha brainwave power, along with improved heart-rate variability, after single BrainTap sessions in healthy young adults and medical students. A separate 12-week trial using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index found meaningful improvements in subjective sleep quality and global sleep scores among a small group of 19 adults, though not every sub-measure, sleep duration among them, shifted significantly. A Brazilian study on day-shift workers with chronic insomnia reported similar gains in sleep latency and total sleep time using an open-loop version of the device. Separately, a 100-volunteer trial conducted through Porter's own Integrative Wellbeing Institute found that a single 20-minute session raised HRV markers by over 20% and cut a measured stress index by 38%, a genuine and reproducible physiological signature of relaxation, though that particular study hasn't been peer-reviewed or published in an indexed journal. Dr. Aruna Viswanathan, chancellor, R.A.R.E Lifecare, who also heads the BrainTap India initiative, cites a personal use-case. She said she can see the effect on her 90-year old mother who has been using BrainTap for six months now. “Her sleep quality has improved greatly, she sleeps more deeply now,” said Dr Viswanathan.The clinical backbone of the India rollout comes from Dr Jamuna Rajeswaran, former head of clinical psychology at NIMHANS, who has run a neurofeedback practice there since 2007, treating over 5,000 patients, and publishing peer-reviewed work applying a modified, sound-only version of the protocol to stroke rehabilitation, after an institutional ethics committee flagged the light component as carrying a small seizure risk in a photosensitive minority. She has since extended the work, on a smaller and still-unpublished scale, to adult ADHD and clinical depression, and is now beginning a pilot with autistic children. "We've submitted a proposal to Ramachandra University last month for a certification programme," she said. "We're looking at psychologists and social workers, people who already understand the brain, and building the training from the anatomy up."For now, though, what launches in India on Saturday is positioned strictly as a wellness product rather than a medical device, with sleep as its lead consumer use case and the clinical, certification-gated version running as a separate, slower track alongside it. Whether a technology four decades in the making, now repackaged with a thumb sensor and an AI recommendation layer, delivers on its more ambitious claims will likely depend on the kind of independently verified, India-specific research that, by its own backers' admission, is still a work in progress. (registration for the 2-day seminar, starting Aug 15 can be done at “ thelongevitysummitindia.com ”)
Article Summary: BrainTap USA is set to launch in India on Saturday at the two-day Longevity Summit India in Mumbai. The headset delivers pulsed LED light through closed eyelids alongside binaural beats, isochronic tones and guided audio through a companion app. The idea is to shift users out of the anxious, overstimulated "beta" state most people live in.

Article Title: Trump admin accuses over 40 nations including India of helping China evade tariffs - what it means
Article Text:
The report refers to a US Commerce Department estimate that goods worth $67 billion were transshipped through India, Mexico and Vietnam in 2025. (AP photo)

India named

Trump tariff failure?

GTRI identifies 4 key shortcomings

What India should do

A new US report has alleged that India is among 40 countries that are helping China evade Trump’s tariffs with the help of a shadow trans-shipment network. The White House on August 13, 2026, released a 25-page report titled The Great Transshipment Scam: Rise, Scope, and Costs, alleging that Chinese exporters are routing goods through more than 40 countries to bypass higher US tariffs.Prepared by the White House Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy under Peter Navarro, the report argues that while the Section 301 tariffs introduced against China in 2018 reduced direct Chinese exports to the United States, they also gave rise to a worldwide transshipment network.According to the report, Chinese products are being relabelled, repackaged, re-invoiced or subjected to limited processing in countries facing lower US tariff rates before being exported to the United States under a different country of origin. The report describes this system as the “Shadow Transshipment Network.”To illustrate the scale of the issue, the report cites five separate estimates of annual transshipment or related exposure: $40 billion from Goldman Sachs, $60 billion from the White House Council of Economic Advisers, $75 billion from Exiger, $109 billion from the US Commerce Department and $303 billion from Altana. It also notes that these estimates are based on different methodologies and therefore cannot be directly compared.The report classifies more than 40 countries into three separate tiers based on their alleged role in transshipment activities. India has been placed in Tier 1, labelled "Diversified Scale Leaders", alongside Canada, the European Union, Israel, Japan, Mexico, South Korea and Taiwan. According to the report, these economies possess large industrial manufacturing bases where alleged transshipment risks are intertwined with legitimate trade flows.Tier 2, described as "Significant Economic Integration with China", comprises Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Turkey and Vietnam. Tier 3, labelled "Small, Opportunistic Targets", includes Bangladesh, Cambodia, the Philippines, Singapore, Sri Lanka and the UAE.During a media briefing, senior White House trade adviser Peter Navarro specifically referred to India while cautioning that countries could attempt to circumvent higher US tariffs through transshipment as Washington expands its tariff measures."This is about the 40-plus countries that are enabling the transshipping, and as we impose higher tariffs on other countries, India, Vietnam, down the line, they're going to try this transhipment too. Our message is simply that the way to pay less is not to cheat; it is to stop dumping, respect intellectual property, drop your barriers to American goods and move towards reciprocity. Our warning to the lower tariff countries facilitating and enabling the transshipping is this: preferential access to the American market is not a license to launder somebody else's exports," said Navarro.The report refers to a US Commerce Department estimate that goods worth $67 billion were transshipped through India, Mexico and Vietnam in 2025, resulting in tariff losses of $28 billion. However, it does not specify India's share of that estimate, identify any Indian exporter or provide details of a single fraudulent shipment.According to the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), the report also singles out India's Pune-Gujarat-Chennai manufacturing corridor for products classified under HS codes 8413-8414, covering pumps and compressors.However, an analysis by GTRI indicates that India has significant domestic manufacturing capability in these product categories.During FY2026, India exported liquid pumps worth $1.61 billion worldwide, including shipments worth $414.5 million to the United States, while importing liquid pumps valued at $326.4 million from China. Similarly, India exported air pumps and gas compressors worth $1.48 billion globally, of which $335.4 million went to the US, even as imports from China stood at $1.63 billion.Given the scale of India's worldwide exports in these sectors, GTRI argues that it is difficult to assume that shipments to the United States merely consist of Chinese products being rerouted through India.According to GTRI, the new report is a way of shifting focus away from tariff outcomes of the Donald Trump administration.Although US imports from China declined from $525.8 billion in 2017 to $327.5 billion in 2025, America's overall imports continued to rise, increasing from $2.41 trillion to $3.50 trillion over the same period.“The US therefore replaced many Chinese finished goods with imports from other countries rather than with domestic production. Trump’s tariffs changed the source of imports but failed to reduce America’s overall dependence on imported goods,” says GTRI founder Ajay Srivastava.China, meanwhile, appears to have adjusted its export strategy. Instead of relying primarily on direct exports of finished goods to the United States, it has increasingly supplied components and intermediate products to manufacturers in countries such as Mexico, Vietnam, India and several European and Asian economies. These inputs are then processed, assembled or incorporated into finished products before being exported to the US, notes GTRI.“Where such processing results in substantial transformation, these are genuine exports of the manufacturing country and an established feature of global value chains. They cannot be treated as Chinese transshipment merely because they contain Chinese inputs. China has, in effect, responded to US tariffs by strengthening its position as a global supplier of intermediate goods,” GTRI says.The report also points out that aggregate trade figures do not, by themselves, establish widespread rerouting of Chinese exports. Chinese imports may be used for domestic consumption, genuine manufacturing activity or exports to destinations other than the United States.According to GTRI, the report suffers from four major weaknesses.First, it broadens the conventional definition of transshipment, which ordinarily refers to cargo being unloaded and reloaded without alteration, to include activities such as assembly, testing, finishing and component integration. In doing so, it conflates genuine manufacturing with origin fraud and risks portraying legitimate production within global supply chains as transshipment without first establishing any violation.Second, the report relies on trade correlations as evidence. A reduction in direct imports from China accompanied by rising imports from another country does not, by itself, demonstrate that the same goods were simply relabelled and rerouted.Third, GTRI argues that it is the United States' own country-specific tariff structure that has created the large tariff differentials making evasion financially attractive.Fourth, although the United States already applies non-preferential rules of origin based on the principle of substantial transformation, the report argues that these rules remain complex, inconsistent and susceptible to misuse, while recommending stricter statutory standards.India should seek evidence and conduct its own verification, says Ajay Srivastava.GTRI says India should ask the United States to disclose the detailed basis of its allegations, including country-specific, product-level and shipment-level data, as well as India's share of the estimated $67 billion in alleged transshipped goods.It also recommends that India independently examine exports of pumps and compressors by comparing firm-level imports from China with exports to the United States and verifying the extent of domestic value addition. Such an exercise would help identify any misuse, safeguard compliant exporters and enable India to contest unsubstantiated allegations with credible evidence.
Article Summary: The White House on August 13, 2026, released a 25-page report titled The Great Transshipment Scam: Rise, Scope, and Costs. It alleges that Chinese exporters are routing goods through more than 40 countries to bypass higher US tariffs. The report refers to a US Commerce Department estimate that goods worth $67 billion were transshipped through India and Vietnam in 2025.

Article Title: Europe, Without the Middlemen: A Different Way to See the Continent
Article Text:
ORN is building a different model of European travel, one where the company selling your journey is also operating it on the ground.

Why being a direct operator matters

ORN, Europe Journeys

Europe for travellers who want to experience more and worry less

What is the cheapest ticket?

When DIY Europe becomes a logistics exercise

One philosophy, two ways to travel

is for travellers seeking assistance, companionship, predictable costs and the ability to see more of Europe without managing every movement themselves. The people behind ORN

​ ORN Founder & CEO Vinay Gupta

For most Indian travellers, a holiday to Europe begins long before the flight takes off. Countries, hotels, trains, transfers, sightseeing, visas and countless individual bookings somehow have to come together across several cities and countries.But there is one question travellers rarely ask when booking: Who is actually looking after me once I land? ORN was built around that question.Unlike a conventional travel seller, ORN is a direct European operator. It owns a fleet of over 100 coaches and Mercedes vans and operates from 12 offices across Europe. The company selling the journey and the people operating it on the ground are part of the same system.Put simply, ORN doesn’t just send you to Europe. ORN welcomes you there.International holidays can pass through multiple layers before they are finally delivered to the traveller. Every additional layer can add cost and create distance between the customer and the people actually responsible for the experience.ORN’s model is different. By owning and operating European mobility infrastructure at scale, it removes unnecessary layers and spreads operating costs across larger passenger volumes. The objective isn’t to create a cheaper Europe by cutting corners. It is to operate more efficiently, so more of what a traveller pays goes into the journey itself.Direct operation also creates clearer accountability. If plans change or a traveller needs help, the company that made the promise remains connected to the people delivering it.For ORN, that’s the proposition: fewer layers, greater responsibility and better value.Not everyone wants to navigate Europe alone. ORN’s coach journeys are particularly relevant for first-time international travellers, senior citizens, solo travellers, families from India’s Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities and value-conscious travellers who want to see a lot of Europe without spending their holiday managing logistics. For them, luxury can mean something surprisingly practical: not carrying suitcases through unfamiliar stations, searching for platforms, arranging repeated transfers or wondering what happens if a connection is missed.On an organised coach journey, the luggage travels with you, transportation is coordinated, and someone is responsible for what happens next.For a senior traveller, that means assistance. For children sending their parents abroad, reassurance. For a solo traveller, it offers the freedom to travel independently with the security of knowing there is a journey and support system around them.And travelling continuously by road has another advantage: you see the Europe between the cities - Alpine roads, lakes, vineyards, villages and countryside that are easily missed when the holiday becomes a sequence of airports and stations.For the value-led traveller, the question therefore isn’t simply, “” It is: “Independent travel can be wonderful. But anyone who has moved a family and several suitcases through multiple European cities knows that DIY has another side.Check out. Taxi to the station. Find the platform. Move the luggage. Board the train. Arrive. Find another taxi. Reach the next hotel. Wait for check-in. Then do it all again a few days later.Europe’s rail system isn’t the problem. Fragmentation is.The individual ticket may look economical, but the complete journey also includes transfers, taxis, local transportation, luggage movement and something travellers rarely price: their holiday time.Which raises a different question: How much of your Europe holiday are you spending experiencing Europe and how much are you spending operating it?For families and small groups who want independence without the logistical burden of DIY travel, ORN offers another model: a chauffeur-driven Mercedes van across Europe.One family. One vehicle. One chauffeur. One continuous journey.The van collects you from your hotel, your luggage travels with you, and the journey continues from city to city. A scenic village, lake, viewpoint or lunch stop along the way can become part of the holiday rather than another transportation problem.A rental car gives freedom, but someone has to drive. Rail provides connectivity, but the family works around stations and schedules. A chauffeur-driven van provides private road travel without requiring the family to operate it.And economics can be more interesting than they first appear. Compare the van not with one train ticket, but with the- rail fares, station transfers, airport transfers, taxis and local transportation. Article Title: India's forex reserves climb to $707 billion, mark $14.1 billion jump
Article Text:
The jump comes amid strong inflows under the RBI's forex swap measures, which have attracted over $40 billion since June.

India's foreign exchange reserves rose by $14.136 billion to $707.002 billion in the week ended August 7, according to data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday.The reserves had increased by $10.512 billion to $692.866 billion in the previous week ended July 31, as per the data, cited by PTI.India's forex reserves had touched a record $728.494 billion in the week ended February 27 before the onset of the Middle East conflict triggered several weeks of declines. The rupee came under pressure during the period, prompting the RBI to intervene in the foreign exchange market through dollar sales.For the week ended August 7, foreign currency assets (FCAs), the largest component of India's reserves, rose by $9.946 billion to $574.625 billion, RBI data showed.FCAs, when expressed in dollar terms, also reflect the impact of appreciation or depreciation of non-US currencies such as the euro, pound and yen held in the reserves.Gold reserves increased by $3.995 billion to $108.738 billion during the week.Special drawing rights (SDRs) rose by $79 million to $18.745 billion, while India's reserve position with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) increased by $116 million to $4.894 billion.The rise in reserves comes after the RBI and the government launched measures in July, including the FCNR(B) deposit scheme, to attract foreign exchange inflows. India has so far received about $40 billion under these measures, according to reports.
Article Summary: India's forex reserves had touched a record $728.494 billion in the week ended February 27 before the onset of the Middle East conflict triggered several weeks of declines. The rise in reserves comes after the RBI and the government launched measures in July, including the FCNR(B) deposit scheme.

Article Title: 'Declared unruly': IndiGo on woman who damaged property worth Rs 49k at Bhubaneswar airport
Article Text:
A woman passenger was declared “unruly” after allegedly damaging airport equipment worth Rs 49,000 following an IndiGo flight cancellation in Bhubaneswar.

NEW DELHI: IndiGo on Friday said that a woman passenger was declared “unruly” and handed over to security agencies after allegedly damaging airport property worth Rs 49,000 following the cancellation of a flight from Bhubaneswar to Kolkata due to a technical snag.In a statement, IndiGo said flight 6E 7352, scheduled to operate from Bhubaneswar to Kolkata on August 13, was cancelled after a technical issue was detected during the aircraft’s mandatory pre-departure inspection."IndiGo flight 6E 7352, scheduled to operate from Bhubaneswar to Kolkata on August 13, 2026, was cancelled due to a technical snag identified during the mandatory pre-departure inspection of the aircraft," the IndiGo spokesperson said in a statement."We regret the inconvenience caused to our customers and took all efforts to minimise the same including offering them regular updates, refreshments, accommodation and alternate travel options or full refunds as applicable. During this, one of the customers who caused damage to the airport property was declared unruly and handed over to relevant security agencies in line with standard operating procedures," the statement read.The alleged incident took place around 6pm at Biju Patnaik International Airport's departure lounge in the presence of Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), IndiGo and Airports Authority of India (AAI) officials.The AAI alleged the woman damaged a monitor, keyboard and passport-swiping machine, causing an estimated loss of Rs 49,000.A video purportedly showing the incident has also surfaced on social media. The footage shows a heated altercation at the airport and alleged damage to airport infrastructure following the flight cancellation.
Article Summary: A woman passenger was declared ‘unruly’ and handed over to security agencies. She allegedly damaged airport property worth Rs 49,000 following the cancellation of a flight from Bhubaneswar to Kolkata. IndiGo said flight 6E 7352 was cancelled after a technical issue was detected.

Article Title: Rajasthan UCC draft Bill mandates marriage registration within 60 days
Article Text:
Law minister Jogaram Patel and PHED minister Kanhaiya Lal addressing the media after Cabinet meeting





JAIPUR: Rajasthan ’s proposed Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026, will make registration of all marriages mandatory within 60 days of solemnisation, while allowing people of all religions and communities to marry according to their customs, including Saptapadi, Nikah, Anand Karaj and Holy Union.The draft Rajasthan Uniform Civil Code (Saman Nagrik Sanhita) Bill, 2026, approved by the state Cabinet Thursday, will be introduced in the upcoming Assembly session.Govt said the Bill has been framed in keeping with the spirit of Article 44 of the Constitution and seeks to create a uniform legal framework for marriage, divorce, inheritance, maintenance and live-in relationships.The proposed law will not apply to Scheduled Tribes. According to its provisions, marriage registration has been made mandatory and polygamy prohibited.Under the draft Bill, failure to register a marriage can attract a fine of up to Rs 10,000. If the requirement is ignored despite notice, the fine can go up to Rs 25,000. A registrar who deliberately delays or neglects registration process may also face a fine of up to Rs 25,000.Non-registration or delayed registration, however, will not make a marriage invalid.The Bill requires the registrar to issue a registration certificate or reject an application with written reasons within 15 days of receiving the memorandum for registration of marriage or divorce.If an application is rejected, an appeal can be filed before the Registrar General within 30 days. The appeal must be decided within 60 days.Govt departments, semi-govt companies, public undertakings and local bodies will be allowed to change an employee’s marital status in service records only after an authorised marriage certificate is submitted.The draft also brings live-in relationships under a formal legal framework. Partners will have to submit written intimation or register the start and termination of a live-in relationship, with the stated aim of protecting the rights of both parties.Bill provides for courts to declare a marriage null or void on grounds including violation of the Code, consent obtained through force or fraud, impotence and other prescribed reasons.It also lays down a uniform framework for succession when a person dies without leaving a will. Property will pass to legal heirs in three categories.The first category includes the surviving spouse, surviving children, spouses and children of deceased children, and parents.The second includes step-parents, brothers and sisters, spouses and children of deceased siblings, siblings of parents, and paternal and maternal grandparents. The third covers other relatives not included in the first two categories.If no legal heir is found in any of the three categories, the property will devolve to the govt, which will also assume the liabilities and obligations attached to it.A child in the womb at the time of a person’s death will have full inheritance rights if subsequently born alive.The draft was prepared on recommendations of an expert committee headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai.The committee held divisional-level public hearings and consulted citizens, public representatives, religious leaders and legal experts.
Article Summary: The draft Rajasthan Uniform Civil Code (Saman Nagrik Sanhita) Bill, 2026, approved by the state Cabinet Thursday. It will be introduced in the upcoming Assembly session. The proposed law will not apply to Scheduled Tribes. Marriage registration has been made mandatory and polygamy prohibited.

Article Title: Delhi traffic restrictions on Independence Day: Check key road closures, bus diversions for Aug 15
Article Text:
Delhi police conduct vehicle checking at the Aya Nagar Border as security arrangements intensify across national capital ahead of Independence Day , in New Delhi on Thursday.





NEW DELHI: The Delhi Traffic Police has issued a detailed traffic advisory ahead of the Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort on August 15, with several roads to remain closed to general traffic and restrictions on buses and commercial vehicles.The restrictions will be in place primarily from 4am to 10am on August 15 for security and traffic management around the Red Fort. Only vehicles carrying valid parking labels will be permitted on several restricted stretches.Among the major roads that may be avoided during the restricted hours are Netaji Subhash Marg from Delhi Gate to Chatta Rail Chowk, Lothian Road between GPO Delhi and Chatta Rail Chowk, SP Mukherjee Marg between HC Sen Marg and Yamuna Bazar Chowk, Chandni Chowk Road from Fountain Chowk to Red Fort and Ring Road between Rajghat and ISBT.The traffic police has suggested alternative routes for motorists travelling between north and south Delhi. One route is via Aurobindo Marg, Safdarjung Road, Kamal Ataturk Marg, Kautilya Marg, Sardar Patel Marg, 11 Murti, Mother Teresa Crescent, Park Street, Mandir Marg, Panchkuian Road and Rani Jhansi Road. Another route is through Connaught Place, Minto Road, Bhavbhuti Marg, Ajmeri Gate, Shradhanand Marg, Lahori Gate Chowk, Naya Bazar and SP Mukherjee Marg.Traffic restrictions will also affect city and interstate buses. Buses bound for Kauria Pul, Red Fort and Old Delhi Railway Station will be diverted through the ISBT Bridge and will terminate at Boulevard Road near the Mori Gate U-turn. Buses heading towards New Delhi, Connaught Place and Central Secretariat will use the ISBT Bridge, Boulevard Road, Rani Jhansi Flyover, Rani Jhansi Road and Mandir Marg.Buses travelling towards South Delhi from the ISBT side will follow the diverted route up to Mandir Marg before proceeding through Shankar Road, Upper Ridge Road, Simon Bolivar Marg and Dhaula Kuan.Several buses normally terminating at Old Delhi Railway Station, Red Fort, Jama Masjid and Kauria Pul will be curtailed or diverted. Buses coming from Roshanara Road towards Old Delhi Railway Station will terminate opposite the State Bank of India inside Tis Hazari Court, while buses from Old Rohtak Road towards Old Delhi Railway Station and Red Fort will terminate at Mori Gate.The advisory also states that all private and mini buses will terminate at the MCD car parking area at Mori Gate. Gokhale Road will operate one-way from Mori Gate towards Kashmiri Gate and the Gokhale Market 'T' Point.Restrictions on commercial transport and interstate buses will also be enforced. Goods vehicles will not be permitted between Nizamuddin Khatta and Wazirabad Bridge from midnight on August 14 until 11am on August 15. Interstate buses will not be allowed between Maharana Pratap ISBT and Sarai Kale Khan ISBT during the same period.Local city buses, including DTC buses, will also face restrictions on the Ring Road between ISBT Kashmiri Gate and the NH-24/NH-9 junction at Nizamuddin Khatta from midnight on August 14 until 11am on August 15. Several other roads, including Lothian Road, Netaji Subhash Marg, SP Mukherjee Marg, parts of Ring Road, Mathura Road and Vikas Marg, will also be closed to inter-city and DTC buses during this period.Normal bus services are expected to resume after 11am on August 15. The traffic police has advised commuters to leave early to avoid last-minute congestion and inconvenience.The advisory also lists restrictions for pedestrians and visitors attending the Independence Day ceremony. The public has been advised not to carry cameras, binoculars, remote-control car keys, umbrellas, handbags, briefcases, transistors, cigarette lighters, tiffin or lunch boxes and water bottles. People have also been asked not to touch suspicious objects and to immediately alert the nearest police officer about any suspicious movement or unidentified object.The flying of paragliders, paramotors, hang gliders, UAVs, microlight aircraft, remotely piloted aircraft, hot-air balloons, quadcopters and similar aerial platforms has also been prohibited over Delhi during the specified security period.For commuters travelling to important locations, the advisory provides separate routes to Old Delhi Railway Station, New Delhi Railway Station and ISBT Kashmere Gate from different parts of the city.The Delhi Traffic Police has also arranged DTC recovery vans from 5am on August 15 until the diversions are cleared at Gokhale Marg, Ghata Masjid, Yamuna Bazar, Delhi Gate and Chatta Rail Chowk.Commuters have been advised to plan their journeys in advance and use the suggested alternative routes during the Independence Day traffic restrictions.
Article Summary: Several roads to remain closed to general traffic and restrictions on buses and commercial vehicles. Restrictions will be in place primarily from 4am to 10am on August 15 for security and traffic management around the Red Fort. Only vehicles carrying valid parking labels will be permitted on several restricted stretches.
